anomalies.observed: The net /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW contains only the anodes of D4, D14 and D23 and has no supply or driver anywhere else in the netlist.
anomalies.expected: The LED anodes must be connected to a 3.3 V source or controlled LED-power rail so that the LEDs can illuminate when their cathodes are pulled low.
anomalies.impact: D4, D14 and D23 have floating anodes, so these LEDs will never turn on. This disables the associated Ethernet/status LED indications.

anomalies.observed: D30 pin 4 (A2) is on ESTOP_OUT, and D30 pin 2 (K2) connects through R60 back to ESTOP_OUT. Thus the second LED in D30 has both anode and cathode pulled to the same net.
anomalies.expected: The second LED should have a current path to ground, typically via R60 to GND, analogous to the first LED’s R59-to-GND path. It should indicate ESTOP_OUT state, not be connected across itself.
anomalies.impact: The second D30 LED is effectively shorted out through R60 and cannot light. The e-stop status indication provided by that LED is lost.

anomalies.observed: C13 is a 0603 decoupling capacitor but its Value field is "0.1mF 50V" (0.1 millifarad = 100 µF). Its description and MPN specify a 100 nF X7R 0603 capacitor.
anomalies.expected: The value should be 0.1 µF / 100 nF, matching the description, footprint, and selected MPN CC0603KRX7R9BB104.

evidence.quote: (description " 50V 100nF X7R ±10% 0603 Multilayer Ceramic Capacitors MLCC - SMD/SMT ROHS")

anomalies.impact: If the Value field is used for procurement or assembly, a 100 µF capacitor would be incorrectly specified in an 0603 footprint. Even as a schematic label, this is a 1000× error on a decoupling capacitor and can cause incorrect BOM/assembly behavior.

parsed.summary: The design files contain several concrete deviations: the /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW net floats the anodes of three LEDs, D30’s second LED is wired with both ends on ESTOP_OUT, and C13’s value is 1000× larger than its description/MPN. These would leave status LEDs nonfunctional and can cause incorrect assembly of C13.
